key_insight: Canonical lifted-product quantum LDPC codes can be co-designed with a matching logical basis to enable a full, structured, and low-overhead instruction set for fault-tolerant computation.
engineering_relevance: This makes high-rate qLDPC architectures more practical by replacing generic, hard-to-scale logical operations with modular gates, measurements, and surgeries tailored to the code structure.
method: Define a canonical logical basis from cyclic-orbit structure in canonical lifted-product codes.
Use this basis to realize constant-depth automorphism and fold-transversal Clifford gates.
Build modular graph-code surgeries, parallel Pauli-product measurements, and magic-state injection with reusable seed gadgets or a compact extractor.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports concrete constructions for example codes such as [[1122,148,<=20]] and [[4350,1224,<=20]], including only 2 or 4 seed surgery gadgets and a compact extractor smaller than half the data block.
watch_item: The approach is specialized to canonical LP codes with cyclic symmetry, so applicability and circuit overhead may vary for codes outside this structured family.
paper_title: Logical computation with canonical lifted product codes
